mainTopic: Who and what is covered by the Torah's laws against paying wages late, and how each תנא reads the פסוקים
overview: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that reads the פסוק about not oppressing a hired worker word by word. The first תנא puts a גר תושב, and also rented animals and utensils, under all the late-payment laws. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is narrower: a גר תושב is only under 'ביומו תתן שכרו', and animals and utensils are only under 'בל תעשק'. Our משנה fits neither of them fully, so רבא says it follows the school of רבי ישמעאל. The גמרא then explains the dispute. The first תנא links the two פסוקים through the word 'שכיר' ('hired worker'). רבי יוסי does not make that link, and he uses 'כי עני הוא' to leave animals and utensils out of 'ביומו'. Our תנא includes animals and utensils from 'פעולת' and 'אתך', and leaves out the גר תושב from 'רעך'. Finally, the גמרא shows what each opinion learns from the remaining words: paying the poor first, not applying עושק and גזל to a גוי, and רב אסי's rule that even a tiny job counts.

steps.title: Reading the verse: who counts as a protected worker
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads three words of the פסוק. 'מאחיך' leaves out non-Jews, 'גרך' means a גר צדק, and 'בשעריך' means a גר תושב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From your brothers' leaves out others. 'Your stranger' means a righteous convert. 'Within your gates' means a person who eats non-kosher carcasses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing its quote of a ברייתא that explains each word of the פסוק about not oppressing a hired worker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word of the פסוק defines who is protected. A non-Jew is left out. A full convert (גר צדק) is included. A גר תושב is also included, even though he still eats נבילות.

keyTerms.meaning: one who eats meat from animals not properly slaughtered
a non-Jew living in ארץ ישראל who accepted the basic laws but did not fully convert

phrases.english: "From your brothers" – to leave out others.
phrases.notes: The פסוק is דברים 24:14. 'Others' means non-Jews, who are not 'your brothers'.

phrases.english: "Your stranger" – this is a righteous convert.
"Within your gates" – this is one who eats unslaughtered carcasses.
phrases.notes: This is describing a גר תושב, who lives among us but has not fully converted, so he still eats נבילות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא the גמרא began quoting before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר צדק and a גר תושב are protected by the wage laws, and non-Jews are not.

steps.title: What about renting animals and utensils?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know the wage laws also apply to paying rent for animals and utensils, and not only to wages for a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only know about paying a person. From where do I know to include animals and utensils?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a question to set up its next derivation from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words learned so far all describe people. The ברייתא now asks whether rent owed for an animal or an object is covered by the same laws.

keyTerms.meaning: rent paid for animals and utensils

phrases.english: I have only the wages of a person;
from where do we include animals and utensils?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שְׂכַר אָדָם, מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת בְּהֵמָה וְכֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the list of people by asking about non-human rentals.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that rent for animals and utensils is covered by the wage prohibitions.

steps.title: 'In your land' includes everything
steps.stepSummary: The word 'בארצך' teaches that anything in your land is included. So animals and utensils are under all the late-payment prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'in your land', meaning everything in your land. And for all of them, one breaks all these prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question from the word 'בארצך' in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בארצך' is read broadly as 'everything in your land', which brings in animals and utensils. The ברייתא adds that all of these cases, people and rentals alike, fall under every one of the late-payment prohibitions.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "In your land"
– everything that is in your land.
And for all of them one transgresses all these prohibitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בארצך' means everything in your land, so animals and utensils are included in all the prohibitions.

steps.title: The rule: people, animals and utensils are all covered
steps.stepSummary: Based on this reading, the ruling is that wages for a person and rent for an animal or utensil all fall under 'ביומו תתן שכרו' and 'בל תלין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: whether it is wages for a person, rent for an animal, or rent for utensils, 'On his day you shall give his wages' applies, and 'Do not keep a worker's wages overnight' applies.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sums up the practical rule that follows from the reading it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first תנא's bottom line. All three kinds of payment are covered by both the positive command to pay on time and the prohibition against holding wages overnight.

keyTerms.meaning: on his day you shall give his wages
do not keep overnight (a worker's wages)

steps.whatToRemember: According to the first תנא, people, animals and utensils are all under 'ביומו' and 'בל תלין'.

phrases.english: From here they said:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד שְׂכַר אָדָם וְאֶחָד שְׂכַר בְּהֵמָה
phrases.english: Whether the hire of a person or the hire of an animal
or the hire of utensils –
it is subject to "On his day you shall give his wages,"
phrases.notes: דברים 24:15

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם ״בַּל תָּלִין פְּעֻלַּת שָׂכִיר״.
phrases.english: and they are subject to "Do not keep overnight the wages of a hired worker."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the reading of steps 1 to 3 into a practical rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three kinds of payment are under both 'ביומו תתן שכרו' and 'בל תלין'.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה rules that a גר תושב is only under 'ביומו', not 'לא תלין'. Animals and utensils are only under 'בל תעשק'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה says: for a גר תושב, 'On his day you shall give his wages' applies, but 'Do not keep overnight' does not. For animals and utensils, only 'Do not oppress' applies.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא in the ברייתא gives a narrower view than the first תנא on two points.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He limits the first תנא's rule in two places. For a גר תושב, only one of the late-payment laws applies. Renting animals and utensils is not under either late-payment law, only the general ban on oppressing.

keyTerms.meaning: do not oppress (withhold what is owed)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two disputes. On a גר תושב, רבי יוסי drops only 'לא תלין'. On animals and utensils, he drops both late-payment laws and leaves only 'בל תעשק'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:

phrases.aramaic: גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם ״בְּיוֹמוֹ תִּתֵּן שְׂכָרוֹ״,
phrases.english: a ger toshav is subject to "On his day you shall give his wages,"
but is not subject to "Do not keep overnight."
Animals and utensils are not subject to anything
except "Do not oppress" alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first תנא's ruling in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר תושב is only under 'ביומו'. Animals and utensils are only under 'בל תעשק'.

steps.title: Our משנה fits neither opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view our משנה follows. It does not match the first תנא on a גר תושב, and it does not match רבי יוסי on animals and utensils.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is the משנה? If it is the first תנא who explained 'from your brothers', the ruling on a גר תושב is a problem. If it is רבי יוסי, the ruling on animals and utensils is a problem!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its original question about the author of our משנה and shows that neither תנא fits fully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says a גר תושב is not under 'לא תלין', which matches רבי יוסי and not the first תנא. But it puts animals and utensils under 'לא תלין', which matches the first תנא and not רבי יוסי. So the משנה seems to follow each of them on a different point.

keyTerms.meaning: the first תנא, the opening opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's next move: finding a תנא whose view matches our משנה on both points.

phrases.english: Whose is it?
phrases.notes: He means: whose opinion does our משנה follow?

phrases.english: If it is the first tanna of "from your brothers" –
the ger toshav is difficult.

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי – קַשְׁיָא בְּהֵמָה וְכֵלִים!
phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yosei – animals and utensils are difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two opinions of steps 4 and 5 to test our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The attempt to attribute our משנה to one of the two תנאים in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה matches רבי יוסי on a גר תושב but matches the first תנא on animals and utensils, so neither תנא can be its author.

steps.title: רבא: Our משנה follows the school of רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רבא says our משנה follows the תנא of דבי רבי ישמעאל. That source puts animals and utensils under both 'ביומו' and 'לא תלין', and puts a גר תושב only under 'ביומו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This תנא is from the school of רבי ישמעאל. They taught: hiring a person, renting an animal, and renting utensils are all under 'pay him on his day' and 'do not hold back overnight.' A גר תושב is under 'pay him on his day' but not under 'do not hold back overnight.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from step 6. Our משנה follows a third תנא, the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה did not fit the תנא קמא (on a גר תושב), and it did not fit רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה (on animals and utensils). The ברייתא of דבי רבי ישמעאל agrees with the תנא קמא about animals and utensils. It agrees with רבי יוסי about a גר תושב. So it matches the משנה on both points.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the study hall (school) of רבי ישמעאל
Rent paid for using utensils or tools
A non-Jew living in the land who accepted the seven Noahide laws
The prohibition of keeping a worker's wages overnight

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה = the school of רבי ישמעאל. Animals and utensils get both laws. A גר תושב gets only 'ביומו'.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא – תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הוּא,
phrases.english: This tanna is the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael,
as the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Whether the hire of a person,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד שְׂכַר בְּהֵמָה וְאֶחָד שְׂכַר כֵּלִים –
phrases.english: or the rental of an animal, or the rental of utensils,
it is subject to 'On his day you shall give him his wages'
and to 'You shall not keep it overnight.'

phrases.aramaic: גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב – יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם ״בְּיוֹמוֹ תִתֵּן שְׂכָרוֹ״,
phrases.english: A ger toshav is subject to 'On his day you shall give him his wages,'
but he is not subject to 'Do not keep it overnight.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי תַּנָּא – תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 about whose view the משנה follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a third תנא whose view matches the משנה exactly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to fit neither the תנא קמא nor רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows the ברייתא of דבי רבי ישמעאל, which matches both of its rulings.

steps.title: What is the reason of the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the תנא קמא who explained 'מאחיך' and put a גר תושב under all the laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the first תנא, who explained 'from your brothers'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא goes back to the earlier ברייתא. It asks why the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagree, starting with the reason of the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא put a גר תושב, animals and utensils under every late-payment law, including 'לא תלין'. The גמרא wants to know how he gets 'לא תלין' for all of them, since that is the law רבי יוסי leaves out.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (unnamed) תנא in a ברייתא or משנה
'From your brothers', a word in the פסוק of 'לא תעשק'

phrases.english: What is the reason of the first tanna
who explains 'from your brothers'?
phrases.notes: He means the תנא קמא of the earlier ברייתא, who explained the words of 'לא תעשק' (דברים 24:14).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling whose view the משנה follows, the גמרא turns to the reasons behind the ברייתא's dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source the תנא קמא uses to apply all the laws, including 'לא תלין', to a גר תושב, animals and utensils.

steps.title: The תנא קמא learns 'hired worker' from 'hired worker'
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא learns a גזירה שוה from the word 'שכיר' in both פסוקים. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does not learn it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'hired worker' and 'hired worker.' And רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה does not learn 'hired worker' from 'hired worker.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא links two פסוקים because both use the word 'שכיר'. רבי יוסי does not make that link.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'לא תעשק שכיר' includes the stranger and everything in your land. The תנא קמא copies that wide scope over to 'לא תלין פעולת שכיר' through the shared word. רבי יוסי does not make this comparison, so for him 'לא תלין' stays narrower.

keyTerms.meaning: Learns (by comparing one place to another)
Learning a law from the same word appearing in two places

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree about 'לא תעשק'. The argument is only whether its wide scope carries over to 'לא תלין'.

phrases.english: He learns 'hired worker' from 'hired worker.'
phrases.notes: The word appears in 'לא תעשק שכיר' (דברים 24:14) and in 'לא תלין פעולת שכיר' (ויקרא 19:13).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda
does not learn 'hired worker' from 'hired worker.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא uses the גזירה שוה 'שכיר' 'שכיר'. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does not use it.

steps.title: Why aren't animals and utensils at least under 'pay on his day'
steps.stepSummary: Even without the גזירה שוה, why does רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה not put animals and utensils under 'ביומו תתן שכרו'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted he does not learn 'hired worker' from 'hired worker.' But animals and utensils should still be under 'pay him on his day'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי's view. Not using the גזירה שוה explains why 'לא תלין' is missing, but it does not explain why 'ביומו' is missing too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי said animals and utensils are only under 'לא תעשק'. Skipping the גזירה שוה removes 'לא תלין' from them. But 'ביומו תתן שכרו' is in the same section of דברים as 'בארצך', so it should cover animals and utensils anyway. Why doesn't it?

keyTerms.meaning: Granted that... (admitting one point before asking)
Let him be liable / he should be liable

phrases.english: Granted that he does not learn 'hired worker' from 'hired worker,'
for animals and utensils
he should also be liable for 'On his day you shall give him his wages'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the reason given in step 9 and then shows it does not fully explain רבי יוסי's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's ruling that animals and utensils are only under 'בל תעשק'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rejecting the גזירה שוה only removes 'לא תלין'. 'ביומו', which is in the same passage as 'בארצך', should still apply.

steps.title: 'For he is poor' leaves out animals and utensils
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא teaches that 'כי עני הוא' limits 'ביומו' to someone who can become poor or rich. That leaves out animals and utensils.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנניא taught: The verse says, 'and the sun shall not set upon him, for he is poor.' This means someone who can become poor or rich. Animals and utensils are left out, since they cannot become poor or rich.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a ברייתא of רבי חנניא. The same פסוק that teaches 'ביומו' also limits who it covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of 'ביומו' gives a reason: 'כי עני הוא', 'for he is poor'. Only a person can be poor or rich. So this law cannot apply to an animal or a utensil, even though they are 'in your land'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chananya taught:
The verse says:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְלֹא תָבֹא עָלָיו הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ כִּי עָנִי הוּא״ –
phrases.english: 'And the sun shall not set upon him, for he is poor' —
phrases.notes: דברים 24:15

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁהֵן בָּאִין לִידֵי עֲנִיּוּת וַעֲשִׁירוּת,
phrases.english: someone who can come to poverty and wealth;
this leaves out animals and utensils,
which cannot come to poverty and wealth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting phrase in the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ביומו' should cover animals and utensils, because of 'בארצך'.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כי עני הוא' limits 'ביומו' to people, who can be poor or rich.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רבי יוסי leaves animals and utensils with only 'בל תעשק'.

steps.title: What does the תנא קמא do with 'for he is poor'
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא includes animals and utensils under 'ביומו'. So what does he learn from 'כי עני הוא'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first תנא, what does he do with this 'for he is poor'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the תנא קמא. He does not use 'כי עני הוא' to leave out animals, so what does he learn from those words?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We assume every phrase in the תורה teaches something. If the תנא קמא does not use 'כי עני הוא' to leave out animals and utensils, he must use it for some other law.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (what does he learn from it)

phrases.english: And the first tanna,
this 'for he is poor,'
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא, הַאי ״כִּי עָנִי הוּא״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After seeing how רבי יוסי uses 'כי עני הוא', the גמרא asks how the תנא קמא uses it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the תנא קמא learns from 'כי עני הוא'.

steps.title: It teaches to pay a poor worker before a rich one
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא uses 'כי עני הוא' to teach that a poor worker is paid before a rich worker.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase is needed to put a poor person before a rich person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for the תנא קמא, 'כי עני הוא' teaches a different law. If you cannot pay everyone, pay the poor worker first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, the phrase does not limit who is covered. Instead it sets an order of payment. That is why he still includes animals and utensils under 'ביומו'.

phrases.english: That one is needed
to put a poor person before a rich person.
phrases.notes: He means when the employer can't pay all his workers, the poor one gets paid first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כי עני הוא' teaches that a poor worker is paid before a rich one.

steps.title: רבי יוסי learns the poor-first rule from 'do not oppress'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns the poor-first rule from 'לא תעשק שכיר עני ואביון', so 'כי עני הוא' is free for his exclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה learns that from 'You shall not oppress a hired worker who is poor and needy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יוסי also knows the rule of paying the poor first. He learns it from a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יוסי uses 'כי עני הוא' to leave out animals and utensils, one might ask where he gets the poor-first rule. He gets it from the words 'עני ואביון' in 'לא תעשק'. So both sides agree on the law and only disagree about which פסוק teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes out / is learned from

steps.whatToRemember: Both the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי agree that a poor worker is paid first. They only disagree about whether 'כי עני הוא' also leaves out animals and utensils from 'ביומו'.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda:

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא ״מִלֹּא תַעֲשֹׁק שָׂכִיר עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן״ נָפְקָא.
phrases.english: that is learned from 'You shall not oppress a hired worker who is poor and needy.'
phrases.notes: דברים 24:14

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: הָהוּא ״מִלֹּא תַעֲשֹׁק שָׂכִיר עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן״ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken follow-up question: where does רבי יוסי learn the poor-first rule?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי learns the poor-first rule from 'לא תעשק שכיר עני ואביון'.

steps.title: The first תנא uses each verse for a different ordering rule
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא learns one ordering rule from each verse: a poor worker before a rich one, and a poor worker before a destitute one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא? One verse is for putting a poor person before a rich person, and one is for putting a poor person before a destitute person.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 14 said that 'לא תעשק שכיר עני ואביון' teaches 'poor first'. Here the גמרא explains how the תנא קמא can use both verses: each one teaches a different rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both verses are about putting the poor worker first, so it looks like one of them is extra. The תנא קמא answers that there are two different comparisons. One verse puts a poor worker before a rich one. The other puts a poor worker before an אביון, someone who has nothing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a teaching
To put first, to give priority
A destitute person, poorer than an עני

phrases.english: And the first tanna?
phrases.notes: He is asking: why does the תנא קמא need the second verse too?

phrases.english: One verse is to put a poor person before a rich person,
and one is to put a poor person before a destitute person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא: חַד לְהַקְדִּים עָנִי לְעָשִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers how the תנא קמא uses 'לא תעשק שכיר עני ואביון', since step 14 used that verse for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's poor-first rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the תנא קמא learn from the second verse about the poor?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One verse puts a poor worker before a rich one, and the other puts a poor worker before a destitute one.

steps.title: Why both ordering rules are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that neither rule could be learned from the other, so the תורה had to teach both.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are needed. If the תורה taught only about the destitute person, I would say the reason is that he is not embarrassed to demand his money. But a rich person, who is embarrassed to demand it, I would say does not come after the poor worker. And if the תורה taught only about the rich person, I would say the reason is that he does not need the money. But a destitute person, who does need it, I would say does not come after the poor worker. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the two rules from step 15 are both necessary. You could not figure out either one from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The destitute worker has no shame and will keep asking, so he can wait. But maybe the rich worker, who is too embarrassed to ask, should not be pushed back. The rich worker does not need the money now, so he can wait. But maybe the destitute worker, who badly needs it, should not be pushed back. Each case has its own reason, so each rule needs its own verse.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed; both teachings are necessary
To demand it, to ask for his money

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up עני and אביון. Here the אביון is the poorest of all, and the plain עני still comes before him.

phrases.english: And both are necessary,
for if it had taught us only about the destitute person,
I would say that is because he is not embarrassed to demand it.
But a rich person, who is embarrassed to demand it,
I might say not.
And if it had taught us only about the rich person,
I would say that is because he does not need it,
but a destitute person, who does need it,
I might say not. So both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hidden question of step 15: maybe one rule could be learned from the other.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each verse teaches something the other could not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One ordering rule might have been enough to teach the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each case has its own reason, so both verses are needed.
steps.whatToRemember: For the תנא קמא, the poor worker is paid before both the rich worker and the destitute worker, and each rule comes from its own verse.

steps.title: A two-sided challenge to the תנא of our משנה
steps.stepSummary: Either he uses the 'שכיר' link and should include the גר תושב, or he does not and has no source for animals and utensils.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא, whichever way you look at it: if he learns the link between 'שכיר' and 'שכיר', then the גר תושב should be included too. If he does not learn that link, where does he get animals and utensils from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the תנא of our משנה. It traps him with a 'whichever way you look at it' challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה puts animals and utensils under לא תלין, but not the גר תושב. If he links the two 'שכיר' verses with a גזירה שוה, the גר תושב should carry over too. If he does not link them, there seems to be no source for including animals and utensils under לא תלין.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא, the author of our משנה
Whichever way you look at it
A non-Jew who lives in the land and keeps the seven Noahide laws
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And our tanna: whichever way you look at it?
If he learns 'hired worker' from 'hired worker',
phrases.notes: This is the גזירה שוה linking the two verses about a שכיר, one in ויקרא and one in דברים.

phrases.english: then even a ger toshav should also be included,
and if he does not learn 'hired worker' from 'hired worker',
from where does he get animals and utensils?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא's opinions to the ruling of our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of our משנה: animals and utensils are under לא תלין, but the גר תושב is not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma. Using the גזירה שוה would include too much, the גר תושב. Not using it would leave no source for animals and utensils.

steps.title: 'אתך' includes anything whose work is with you
steps.stepSummary: Our תנא does not use the 'שכיר' link. He includes animals and utensils from the extra word 'אתך', with you, in the verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: In fact he does not learn 'שכיר' from 'שכיר'. It is different there, because the verse says: 'The wages of a hired worker shall not stay with you until morning.' This means anything whose work is with you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks the second side of the dilemma. It shows a different source for animals and utensils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse adds the extra word 'אתך', with you. As Rashi explains, that covers anything whose work is with you, including a rented animal or utensil. That makes the גזירה שוה unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not let it stay overnight

phrases.english: Really, he does not learn 'hired worker' from 'hired worker',
and it is different there, because the verse says:
phrases.notes: 'There' means the לא תלין law. ויקרא 19:13

phrases.english: 'The wages of a hired worker shall not stay overnight'
'with you until morning':
anything whose work is with you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second side of the dilemma in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new source from a word in the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the גזירה שוה, there seemed to be no source for animals and utensils.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'פעולת' includes anything whose work you used, so animals and utensils are included without the גזירה שוה.

steps.title: Then the גר תושב should be included too
steps.stepSummary: If anything whose work is with you is included, the גר תושב's work is with you too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even a גר תושב should be included too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer just given. Its broad reading of 'פעולת' seems to include too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר תושב also does work for you. So the broad reading of 'פעולת' should put him under לא תלין, but our משנה says he is not.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב נָמֵי!
phrases.english: If so, even a ger toshav should also be included!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the broad reading of 'פעולת' from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'anything whose work is with you'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading also covers the גר תושב, which goes against our משנה.

steps.title: 'רעך' leaves out the גר תושב
steps.stepSummary: The same verse says 'your neighbor', which leaves out the גר תושב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'your neighbor', meaning your neighbor and not a גר תושב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the same verse. The word 'רעך' limits the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse begins 'לא תעשק את רעך', do not hold back from your neighbor. 'Your neighbor' does not include a גר תושב. So 'פעולת' brings in animals and utensils, and 'רעך' keeps the גר תושב out. This fits our משנה exactly.
steps.whatToRemember: For our משנה, 'פעולת' includes animals and utensils under לא תלין, and 'רעך' leaves out the גר תושב, without any גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: The verse says 'your neighbor':
phrases.notes: This is earlier in the same verse: 'לא תעשק את רעך', ויקרא 19:13.

phrases.english: your neighbor, and not a ger toshav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the law with another word in the same verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'פעולת' would include the גר תושב too.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'רעך' leaves out the גר תושב, so only animals and utensils are added.

steps.title: If 'your neighbor' excludes, animals and utensils should be excluded too
steps.stepSummary: If רעך leaves out the גר תושב, it should also leave out animals and utensils, since they are not 'your neighbor' either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then animals and utensils should also be left out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. If the word רעך cuts out the גר תושב, it should also cut out animals and utensils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 used רעך to exclude the גר תושב. But an animal or a utensil is not 'your neighbor' either. So the same word should exclude them, and that clashes with step 18, where they were included.

phrases.english: If so,
then even animals and utensils too should be excluded!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ בְּהֵמָה וְכֵלִים נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 20 by stretching its logic.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using רעך to exclude the גר תושב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Animals and utensils are not 'your neighbor' either, so the exclusion should reach them too.

steps.title: The word 'with you' brings animals and utensils back in
steps.stepSummary: The word אתך includes everything whose work is with you, so animals and utensils are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'with you'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק also says אתך ('with you'), and that word includes animals and utensils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two words pulling in opposite directions. רעך limits the rule, and אתך widens it. אתך is what keeps animals and utensils inside the איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: With you, a word in the פסוק that widens the rule

phrases.english: But it is written: "with you."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to another word in the פסוק that includes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רעך should exclude animals and utensils too.
steps.terutzMaskana: אתך includes them, so they stay inside the איסור.

steps.title: Why include animals and exclude the גר תושב, and not the reverse?
steps.stepSummary: With one word including and one excluding, how do we know which cases go where?
steps.simpleTranslation: What did you see to include animals and utensils, and to leave out a גר תושב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we decided that אתך includes animals and utensils while רעך excludes the גר תושב. Maybe it should be the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once one word includes and another excludes, we need a reason for assigning each case. Without a reason, the split looks random.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? (Why did you choose this way?)

phrases.english: What did you see to include animals and utensils
and to exclude a resident alien?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the way step 22 split the cases between the two words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of which case each word applies to
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing has been said yet to justify this split over the reverse one.

steps.title: Animals and utensils count as your neighbor's property
steps.stepSummary: Animals and utensils belong to your neighbor, so they still fall under רעך. A גר תושב does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense to include animals and utensils, because they are part of your neighbor's property. A גר תושב is not part of your neighbor's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a reason. Renting your neighbor's animal or utensil still connects to רעך, because they are his property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Renting an animal or a utensil means paying its Jewish owner, so 'your neighbor' is still involved. A גר תושב is a person in his own right and does not belong to any Jew. So he is the one left out.
steps.whatToRemember: Our תנא includes animals and utensils (from פעולת and אתך, since they are your neighbor's property) and excludes the גר תושב (from רעך).

phrases.aramaic: מִסְתַּבְּרָא בְּהֵמָה וְכֵלִים הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹת –
phrases.english: It stands to reason that he should include animals and utensils,
since they are included in your neighbor's property,

phrases.aramaic: גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב אֵינוֹ בִּכְלַל מָמוֹן רֵעֲךָ.
phrases.english: while a resident alien is not included in your neighbor's property.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא בְּהֵמָה וְכֵלִים הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 with a reason based on logic.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The split between the two words might just as well go the other way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Animals and utensils are linked to your neighbor as his property, and a גר תושב is not.

steps.title: How do the other תנאים use the word 'your neighbor'?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא who learns from מאחיך does not need רעך for the גר תושב, so what does he learn from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first תנא who learns from 'from your brothers' (and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה), what do they do with this word 'your neighbor'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other opinions in the ברייתא. They do not use רעך the way our תנא does, so it asks what that word teaches them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word of the תורה should teach something. Since these תנאים do not use רעך to exclude the גר תושב, the גמרא looks for what they learn from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (unnamed) opinion in a ברייתא
From your brothers, a word in the פסוק about a hired worker
What do they do with it (what do they learn from it)?

phrases.english: And the first tanna, who learns from "from your brothers"
phrases.notes: דברים 24:14

phrases.english: [and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda],
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in square brackets, so the question goes to both of them.

phrases.english: what do they do with this word "your neighbor"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:13

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא דְּ״מֵאַחֶיךָ״ הַאי ״רֵעֲךָ״ מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from our תנא to the other opinions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the other תנאים learn from the word רעך

steps.title: 'Your neighbor' comes to exclude a גוי
steps.stepSummary: They use רעך for a ברייתא that says the rule is about your neighbor and not a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for what was taught in a ברייתא: 'your neighbor', and not a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these תנאים use רעך to teach that a גוי is not covered by this איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the word does teach something for them. It excludes a גוי instead of a גר תושב.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: That word is needed for what was taught in a baraita:
"Your neighbor," and not a gentile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.

steps.title: But a גוי is already left out by 'your brothers'
steps.stepSummary: מאחיך already excludes a גוי, so רעך should not be needed for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גוי is already learned from 'your brothers'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that the word מאחיך already leaves out a גוי, so using רעך for the same thing repeats it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two words should not teach the exact same thing. If מאחיך already excludes a גוי, then רעך looks extra for these תנאים.

phrases.english: A gentile is already derived from "your brothers"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using רעך to exclude a גוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מאחיך already teaches this, so רעך would be extra.

steps.title: One word for withholding wages, one for stealing
steps.stepSummary: One word permits withholding a גוי's wages and the other permits stealing from him. This תנא holds that גזל גוי is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: One word permits withholding his wages, and the other permits stealing from him. This תנא holds that stealing from a גוי is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two words teach two different things about a גוי. One is about עושק, and the other is about גזל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עושק means holding back money you owe him, like his wages. גזל means taking something that is already his. Since this תנא holds גזל גוי מותר, he needs one word for each case.

keyTerms.meaning: Withholding what you owe him, like wages

phrases.english: One is to permit withholding what is owed him,
and one is to permit stealing from him,
and he holds that stealing from a gentile is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד לְמִשְׁרֵא עוֹשְׁקוֹ, וְחַד לְמִשְׁרֵא גְּזֵלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 by giving each word its own job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two words between two separate cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both words teach the same exclusion of a גוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: One word covers עושק and the other covers גזל, according to this תנא's view.

steps.title: Why both cases had to be taught
steps.stepSummary: Neither case could be learned from the other, so both words are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If we were only taught about stealing, we might say it is allowed because the גוי did not work for him, but withholding wages after he worked is not allowed. If we were only taught about withholding wages, we might say it is allowed because the money never reached the gentile's hand, but stealing something already in his hand is not allowed. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why we could not learn one case from the other. Each case has a feature that might make it more lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stealing seems easier to allow because the גוי did no work. Withholding wages seems easier to allow because the money was never in his hand. Since each case has its own reason to be lenient, neither one teaches the other.
steps.whatToRemember: For these תנאים, מאחיך and רעך each teach their own law about a גוי, עושק and גזל. Neither could be learned from the other.

phrases.english: And both are necessary:
For if it had taught us only stealing from him,
I would say that is because he did not toil for it,
phrases.notes: He means the גוי did no work for this money. It was just his.

phrases.english: but withholding his wages, where he toiled for it,
I would say no.
And if it had taught us only withholding his wages,
I would say that is because it never reached his hand,
but stealing from him, where it already reached his hand,
I would say no.
So both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 28 by showing that both words are needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One case could be learned from the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each case has its own reason to be lenient, so both must be written.

steps.title: How does רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה use 'the wages shall not stay overnight'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns from the פסוק of לא תלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, what does he do with this פסוק, 'the wages of a hired worker shall not stay with you overnight until morning'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks what this פסוק teaches according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, since he does not use it the way our תנא does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our תנא used פעולת and אתך from this פסוק to include animals and utensils. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does not learn that from here, so the פסוק needs some other teaching for him.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי ״לֹא תָלִין פְּעֻלַּת שָׂכִיר אִתְּךָ עַד בֹּקֶר״
phrases.english: this verse: "The wages of a hired worker shall not stay with you overnight until morning"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:13

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הַאי ״לֹא תָלִין פְּעֻלַּת שָׂכִיר אִתְּךָ עַד בֹּקֶר״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about another תנא's use of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns from the פסוק of לא תלין

steps.title: Even a tiny job counts, as רב אסי teaches
steps.stepSummary: He uses the פסוק for רב אסי's rule: even hiring someone to pick one cluster of grapes falls under בל תלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for רב אסי's teaching. רב אסי said: even if he hired him only to pick one cluster of grapes, he violates בל תלין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns from this פסוק that even the smallest job is covered by the איסור of delaying wages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him the פסוק is not about animals or utensils. It teaches that the size of the job does not matter. Even a tiny wage must be paid on time.

keyTerms.meaning: The איסור against delaying wages overnight

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule: the איסור of delaying wages applies even to a tiny amount of work.

phrases.english: He needs it for the teaching of Rav Asi.
For Rav Asi said:
Even if he hired him only

phrases.aramaic: לִבְצוֹר לוֹ אֶשְׁכּוֹל אֶחָד שֶׁל עֲנָבִים –
phrases.english: to harvest for him one cluster of grapes,
he violates "do not leave overnight."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches רב אסי's rule that even a tiny job is covered by בל תלין.

steps.title: What about the other תנא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the other תנא (the תנא קמא) learns רב אסי's rule, since he does not take it from לא תלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other תנא, where does he learn this rule from?
steps.whatsHappening: With one short word, the גמרא sets up a question: if the תנא קמא does not use לא תלין for רב אסי's rule, where does he get that rule? This step prepares the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 31 showed that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns רב אסי's rule from לא תלין. The other תנא does not read לא תלין that way, so the גמרא asks where he gets the same rule. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one: here, the other תנא (the תנא קמא)
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: The word וְאִידַּךְ is a whole question by itself. It means: what does the other opinion do with this point? It is not the start of a new statement.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: He means the other opinion: if he doesn't learn רב אסי's rule from לא תלין, where does he get it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's source for רב אסי's rule to the תנא קמא's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source the תנא קמא uses for רב אסי's rule that even a tiny job falls under בל תלין.

steps.title: He learns it from "ואליו הוא נשא את נפשו"
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא learns רב אסי's rule from the phrase "ואליו הוא נשא את נפשו": any work the worker gives himself over to is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: He derives it from "and for it he sets his soul". This means anything for which the worker gives over his soul.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא קמא gets רב אסי's rule from a different פסוק: "ואליו הוא נשא את נפשו" (דברים 24:15).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the worker "sets his soul" on his wages. The גמרא reads this to include any job a worker commits himself to, even picking one cluster of grapes. So both תנאים accept רב אסי's rule; they only disagree about which phrase teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: And for it he sets his soul (דברים 24:15)
He derives it (literally, it comes out from)
Gives over his soul: commits himself fully

steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions agree with רב אסי that even a tiny job falls under בל תלין. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns it from לא תלין, and the תנא קמא learns it from "ואליו הוא נשא את נפשו".
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the rule about a small job is accepted by everyone. Only the source in the פסוק is in dispute, so there is no practical disagreement here.

phrases.english: He derives it from "and for it he sets his soul,"
phrases.notes: דברים 24:15

phrases.english: meaning anything for which he gives over his soul.
phrases.notes: So any work the worker commits himself to counts, even a very small job.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִ״וְאֵלָיו הוּא נֹשֵׂא אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ״ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32 by giving the תנא קמא's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא learns רב אסי's rule from "ואליו הוא נשא את נפשו": anything the worker gives his soul over to, even a small job, is included.
